```plato
    //==
    // # Building a cloth — from a grid
    //
    // The constraint graph of a flat patch, derived from `ClothGrid3D` with no
    // mesh in between. Three families of spring, all with rest lengths read off
    // the grid's own initial geometry:
    //
    //  - STRUCTURAL, between neighbours along each axis: resists stretching.
    //  - SHEAR, along both diagonals of each cell: resists the grid collapsing
    //    into a parallelogram, which structural springs alone allow.
    //  - BEND, between vertices two apart along each axis: resists folding.
    //    On a grid this is the two-away spring rather than a dihedral
    //    constraint, because the pattern is regular enough for it and it costs
    //    one distance projection instead of four gradients. `ClothFromMesh`
    //    below produces the dihedral form.

    // The index of grid vertex (column, row) in the row-major vertex array.
    GridVertexIndex(self: ClothGrid3D, column: Integer, row: Integer): VertexIndex
        => VertexIndex(row * self.ColumnCount + column);

    // The world position of grid vertex (column, row).
    GridPosition(self: ClothGrid3D, column: Integer, row: Integer): Point3D
        => self.Origin + self.ColumnStep * column.ToNumber + self.RowStep * row.ToNumber;

    // The number of vertices the grid has.
    GridVertexCount(self: ClothGrid3D): Integer
        => self.ColumnCount * self.RowCount;

    // Grid vertex n, at rest (previous position equal to position) and free.
    // A non-positive mass gives an inverse mass of zero, i.e. a pinned sheet.
    GridVertex(self: ClothGrid3D, n: Integer, vertexMass: Mass): ClothVertex
    {
        var position = self.GridPosition(n % self.ColumnCount, n / self.ColumnCount);
        return ClothVertex(position, position, SafeDivide(1.0, vertexMass.Kilograms, 0.0), false);
    }

    // Every grid vertex, in row-major order.
    GridVertices(self: ClothGrid3D, vertexMass: Mass): Array<ClothVertex>
        => self.GridVertexCount.MapRange(n => self.GridVertex(n, vertexMass));

    // A distance constraint between two grid vertices, its rest length read off
    // the grid's initial geometry so the patch starts unstretched.
    GridSpring(self: ClothGrid3D, columnA: Integer, rowA: Integer, columnB: Integer, rowB: Integer, compliance: Number)
        : ClothDistanceConstraint
        => ClothDistanceConstraint(
            self.GridVertexIndex(columnA, rowA),
            self.GridVertexIndex(columnB, rowB),
            new Length(self.GridPosition(columnA, rowA).Distance(self.GridPosition(columnB, rowB))),
            compliance);

    // Every spring joining a vertex to the one `step` columns to its right:
    // step 1 is structural, step 2 is bend.
    GridRowSprings(self: ClothGrid3D, step: Integer, compliance: Number): Array<ClothDistanceConstraint>
    {
        var span = (self.ColumnCount - step).Max(0);
        return (span * self.RowCount).MapRange(n =>
            self.GridSpring(n % span, n / span, n % span + step, n / span, compliance));
    }

    // Every spring joining a vertex to the one `step` rows below it: step 1 is
    // structural, step 2 is bend.
    GridColumnSprings(self: ClothGrid3D, step: Integer, compliance: Number): Array<ClothDistanceConstraint>
    {
        var span = (self.RowCount - step).Max(0);
        return (self.ColumnCount * span).MapRange(n =>
            self.GridSpring(n % self.ColumnCount, n / self.ColumnCount,
                            n % self.ColumnCount, n / self.ColumnCount + step, compliance));
    }

    // One of a cell's two diagonals: `diagonal` 0 runs from (column, row) to
    // (column + 1, row + 1), and 1 runs the other way.
    GridShearSpring(self: ClothGrid3D, column: Integer, row: Integer, diagonal: Integer, compliance: Number): ClothDistanceConstraint
        => diagonal == 0
            ? self.GridSpring(column, row, column + 1, row + 1, compliance)
            : self.GridSpring(column + 1, row, column, row + 1, compliance);

    // Both diagonals of every cell.
    GridShearSprings(self: ClothGrid3D, compliance: Number): Array<ClothDistanceConstraint>
    {
        var columns = (self.ColumnCount - 1).Max(0);
        var rows = (self.RowCount - 1).Max(0);
        return (columns * rows * 2).MapRange(n =>
            self.GridShearSpring(n / 2 % columns, n / 2 / columns, n % 2, compliance));
    }

    // The whole spring set: structural, then shear, then bend.
    GridSprings(self: ClothGrid3D, compliance: Number): Array<ClothDistanceConstraint>
        => self.GridRowSprings(1, compliance)
            .Concatenate(self.GridColumnSprings(1, compliance))
            .Concatenate(self.GridShearSprings(compliance))
            .Concatenate(self.GridRowSprings(2, compliance))
            .Concatenate(self.GridColumnSprings(2, compliance));

    // One cell's quadrilateral corner loop, wound counter-clockwise seen from
    // the side the cross product of ColumnStep and RowStep points at.
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Winding, handedness, and normals.
    GridQuad(self: ClothGrid3D, column: Integer, row: Integer): Array<VertexIndex>
        => [self.GridVertexIndex(column, row),
            self.GridVertexIndex(column + 1, row),
            self.GridVertexIndex(column + 1, row + 1),
            self.GridVertexIndex(column, row + 1)];

    // The quadrilateral face table of the whole grid, one row per cell.
    GridFaceLoops(self: ClothGrid3D): Array<Array<VertexIndex>>
    {
        var columns = (self.ColumnCount - 1).Max(0);
        var rows = (self.RowCount - 1).Max(0);
        return (columns * rows).MapRange(n => self.GridQuad(n % columns, n / columns));
    }

    // One half of a cell, split along the (column, row) to (column + 1, row + 1)
    // diagonal and wound to match `GridQuad`.
    GridTriangle(self: ClothGrid3D, column: Integer, row: Integer, half: Integer): TriangleFace
        => half == 0
            ? TriangleFace(self.GridVertexIndex(column, row),
                           self.GridVertexIndex(column + 1, row),
                           self.GridVertexIndex(column + 1, row + 1))
            : TriangleFace(self.GridVertexIndex(column, row),
                           self.GridVertexIndex(column + 1, row + 1),
                           self.GridVertexIndex(column, row + 1));

    // Every cell split into two triangles: the collision and rendering faces
    // `Cloth3D` stores.
    GridTriangles(self: ClothGrid3D): Array<TriangleFace>
    {
        var columns = (self.ColumnCount - 1).Max(0);
        var rows = (self.RowCount - 1).Max(0);
        return (columns * rows * 2).MapRange(n =>
            self.GridTriangle(n / 2 % columns, n / 2 / columns, n % 2));
    }

    // A cloth patch over a rectangular grid, with the quad face table kept so
    // the simulated positions read back out as the same mesh. Every vertex has
    // the same mass and every spring the same compliance; pin the ones that
    // should hang with `WithPinnedGridRow`.
    ClothFromGrid(self: ClothGrid3D, vertexMass: Mass, compliance: Number, thickness: Length): ClothMesh3D
        => ClothMesh3D(
            Cloth3D(
                self.GridVertices(vertexMass),
                self.GridSprings(compliance),
                ClothBendConstraint.NoBendConstraints,
                self.GridTriangles,
                thickness),
            FromRows(self.GridFaceLoops));
```
